TikTok

TikTok tracks your behavior across the internet, not just inside the app. Here are the settings that matter and what they actually do.

TLDR Off-platform tracking via TikTok Pixel, a 2026 privacy policy that added precise GPS collection, no AI training opt-out for US users, and default-on ad targeting across platforms. The data profile extends well beyond what you do in the app.

What They Collect

Keystrokes before you post

TikTok logs what you type in the caption field — even if you delete it and never post.

Tracks you off-platform

The TikTok Pixel fires on thousands of third-party sites. Your web activity is reported back to TikTok whether the app is open or not, and whether you have an account or not.

Added GPS collection in Jan 2026

Precise location was explicitly excluded in the prior policy. The January 2026 update added it for US users.

No AI training opt-out for US users

TikTok's 2026 policy grants a worldwide, irrevocable license to use your content for machine learning. EU users can object. US users cannot.

TikTok collects data in two places: inside the app and outside it.

Inside the app: everything you watch, skip, and replay, and for how long. Searches, likes, comments, shares, saves. Sounds you save. Products you tap in TikTok Shop. Content you draft but delete before posting. The keystrokes you make in the caption field. Your device model, OS, unique device identifiers, and IP address.

Outside the app: TikTok operates a tracking network via the TikTok Pixel and TikTok SDK. Businesses install this code on their websites and apps to use TikTok's advertising tools. When you visit any of those properties, your activity is reported back to TikTok. This happens whether the app is open or not. It happens whether you have a TikTok account or not.

TikTok's January 2026 privacy policy update added two things that were not in the prior policy: precise GPS location collection for US users (the previous policy explicitly excluded this) and explicit collection of AI interaction data, including prompts and content at the pre-upload stage. Both are now covered under TikTok's worldwide, irrevocable license to use your content for developing machine learning models.

US user data is stored on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Oracle holds a 15% equity stake in TikTok's US entity and serves as the exclusive US cloud provider, following the ByteDance divestiture deal closed in January 2026. Oracle also audits TikTok's source code and oversees retraining of the recommendation algorithm on US user data.

The Settings That Matter

Off-TikTok Activity Critical
Default: On ▶
www.tiktok.com/setting › Ads › Your Off-TikTok Activity

This is TikTok's equivalent of Meta's Off-Facebook Activity. Advertisers install TikTok's Pixel or SDK on their websites and apps. When you visit those properties, your activity is reported back to TikTok and used to target ads at you. You can view which advertisers have shared data about you, disconnect individual ones, and clear the activity history once every 24 hours. There is also a 'Disconnect All' option.

Turn off: Tap Disconnect All or disconnect individual advertisers

Note: Disconnecting advertisers stops them from using your off-TikTok data for future targeting. It does not delete what TikTok has already collected or processed. The TikTok Pixel on third-party sites still fires when you visit them. The data still goes to TikTok's servers. The setting controls how that data is applied to your profile, not whether it is sent.

Targeted Ads Outside of TikTok Critical
Default: On ▶
www.tiktok.com/setting › Ads › Targeted Ads

Your TikTok behavioral profile is used to serve you TikTok-informed ads on third-party platforms and websites. Your behavior inside TikTok follows you to other apps and sites. Turning this off tells TikTok not to share your profile data with ad partners for off-platform targeting. On iOS 14.5 and later, denying TikTok's App Tracking Transparency prompt via iPhone Settings overrides this toggle at the OS level.

Turn off: Toggle off; also disable App Tracking Transparency on iPhone

Note: Turning this off stops TikTok from using your data to target ads on other platforms. It does not stop TikTok from building or maintaining your ad profile. Your on-platform behavior is still logged and still used for ads within TikTok.

High

Personalized Ads High
Default: On ▶
www.tiktok.com/setting › Ads › Personalized Ads

Controls whether TikTok uses your in-app behavior to select the ads you see in your For You feed. Watch history, search queries, likes, follows, and engagement patterns all feed into this. With this on, the ads are tuned to what TikTok infers about your interests and intent.

Turn off: Toggle off

Note: Turning this off does not stop TikTok from collecting your behavioral data. The profile still gets built. You see generic ads instead of targeted ones. The data collection is unchanged. The Off-TikTok Activity and location settings need to be addressed separately.

Sync Contacts and Facebook Friends High
Default: Off (prompted during onboarding) ▶
www.tiktok.com/setting › Privacy › Sync contacts and Facebook friends

When enabled, TikTok uploads your phone contacts and Facebook friends list to its servers to find people you know and suggest your account to them. The data is sent regardless of whether any matches are found. TikTok uses this to build social graphs. If you previously synced contacts, tap 'Remove previously synced contacts' to request deletion. The same option exists for Facebook friends.

Turn off: Toggle off; tap Remove previously synced contacts

Note: Removing previously synced contacts deletes them from TikTok's contact-sync database for future use. It does not affect inferences already drawn from that data. Your account may still be suggested to people who synced contacts containing your phone number.

Medium

Suggest Your Account to Others Medium
Default: On ▶
www.tiktok.com/setting › Privacy › Suggest your account to others

TikTok recommends your profile to other users based on your phone number, email, or contacts who have your information. Separate toggles exist for contacts, Facebook friends, and people who open or send links. Each can be disabled independently.

Turn off: Disable all toggles

Note: Turning off all suggestion toggles reduces account recommendations driven by contact data. It does not make your public profile unsearchable or prevent your content from appearing in the For You feed of people you do not know.

Browser Autofill Medium
Default: On ▶
www.tiktok.com/setting › Security and Permissions › User Information

TikTok has its own in-app browser used when you tap links inside the app. This browser can autofill payment information and contact information on sites you visit within TikTok. Separate toggles exist for each. You can also access browser settings by tapping the three-dot menu while on a page inside TikTok's browser.

Turn off: Toggle off; or open links in default browser

Note: Turning off autofill stops TikTok from pre-filling forms in its in-app browser. TikTok's in-app browser can still observe your activity on pages you open inside the app. Autofill and page-level browsing data are separate behaviors.

Connected Apps Medium
Default: Varies ▶
www.tiktok.com/setting › Security and Permissions › Apps and Services Permissions

Third-party apps you have authenticated with your TikTok account via TikTok login. Each may have ongoing access to your profile, follower list, and in some cases content permissions. TikTok's Security Checkup tool, also in the Security and Permissions menu, walks through connected apps as part of an account review.

Turn off: Revoke access for unused apps

Note: Revoking a connected app's permissions stops future access. It does not delete data the app already collected before revocation.

Who Gets Your Data

ByteDance
TikTok's parent company, headquartered in Beijing. Following the USDS deal closed in January 2026, ByteDance holds a 19.9% minority stake in TikTok's US entity. US user data is stored on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, not ByteDance servers, as part of a governance framework designed to address regulatory concerns about potential Chinese government access. Oracle provides independent audits. Whether this arrangement fully resolves data sovereignty concerns is subject to ongoing regulatory and policy debate.
TikTok Ad Partners (DSPs and Ad Networks)
TikTok operates a demand-side advertising platform. Brands and agencies buy ads through it. Your behavioral profile is used to match you to campaigns. Advertisers do not receive your raw data directly, but they benefit from TikTok's targeting capabilities, which are built from it. Audience segments and behavioral signals are shared with demand-side platform partners for programmatic campaign delivery and optimization.
The TikTok Pixel Ecosystem
Thousands of websites and apps have TikTok's tracking code installed, either for their own advertising or as part of TikTok Shop integrations. Every time you visit one of those properties, an event fires that reports your activity back to TikTok. Retailers, news publishers, apps, and e-commerce platforms are all part of this ecosystem. You do not need a TikTok account for this to happen. The pixel fires regardless.
Third-Party Measurement Partners
Companies like AppsFlyer, Adjust, and Branch receive data to attribute ad conversions. When you see a TikTok ad and later install an app or make a purchase, that conversion signal travels through these partners back to the advertiser. Your activity on other apps, particularly install and purchase events, feeds into this pipeline.

What They Know About You

After a few weeks of normal use, TikTok has a detailed record of your interests built from watch behavior, not just likes. A video you watched twice with sound on counts for more than one you liked and scrolled past. It knows what you skip at two seconds. It knows what you replay. It knows your search history, your TikTok Shop tap history, and which products you lingered on in ads.

Through off-platform tracking, TikTok also receives data from websites you visit after closing the app. If you browsed a mattress brand, a credit card comparison site, or a car dealership, and any of those sites have TikTok's Pixel installed, TikTok logged it. Combined with device identifiers, precise location, and the social graph built from your contact list, that is a behavioral profile granular enough to predict purchasing intent by category.

That is not a hypothetical. That is what the ad targeting system is designed to produce.

⚠ No AI Training Opt-Out for US Users

As of March 2026, TikTok does not offer US users an opt-out from having their data used to train AI models. TikTok's 2026 privacy policy explicitly names AI interactions, prompts, and pre-upload content as collected data, and grants TikTok a worldwide, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use content for developing machine learning models. EU users retain stronger protections under GDPR and can object to this use. No equivalent mechanism exists for US users at this time.
